Committee: Education Policy
Sponsor: Shelnutt
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 02/08/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 66 as introduced would change the membership of the University of Montevallo Board of Trustees to include the appointment of one at-large nonresident trustee which could increase travel reimbursement costs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of meetings attended by the nonresident trustee and the distance traveled.
Tim Melson, Chairperson
Education Policy

Committee: Education Policy
Sponsor: Shelnutt
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 04/20/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 66 as passed the Senate allows an at-large nonresident to serve as one of the current eleven non-exofficio board member positions on the University of Montevallo Board of Trustees, which could increase travel reimbursement costs of the board by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of meetings attended by the nonresident trustee and the distance traveled.
Terri Collins, Chair
Education Policy

Committee: Finance and Taxation Education
Sponsor: Barfoot
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 04/14/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 231 as introduced would provide an individual income tax deduction, up to $5,000 annually, on contributions made, on or after January 1, 2021, to an Alabama Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) account. Based upon the number of existing accounts, this could reduce receipts deposited into the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $90,000 annually.
As amended and reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education, the provisions of this bill would sunset on December 31, 2025, unless extended by an act of the Legislature.
Arthur Orr, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation Education
